apply.problems:
apply_kb.py pitfalls: errors=4, all with "the row changed since it was read" (the linked verdict's old_line was not found). The four IDs: item-aim-select-mode-vs-use-target, link-animation-off-ailment-immunity, link-physical-xp-last-blow-only, link-stale-skip-save-prompt-flag.

Cause of three of them: each link-* verdict points at a row that another verdict in the same run adds: two-physical-resolvers-not-mergeable, physical-xp-credit-assigned-not-added and title-skip-save-prompt-set-on-cancel. The verdict files are applied in sorted-ID order, so every "link-*" runs before its row has been inserted. In the first run all three links were refused and the three rows went in without the known_bugs link.

item-aim-select-mode-vs-use-target is a real mismatch. Its old_line is not in rebuild_info/pitfalls.md, either before or after its link.

Script bug (apply_kb.py): the pitfalls step is NOT idempotent when a link targets a row added in the same batch. On a rerun the link rewrites the added row X into the linked N. Then the "added" check no longer finds X and inserts X again, so every rerun adds one more copy.

My own mistake, now undone: while trying to get back the output that got cut off, I ran the pitfalls step twice more. One was a PowerShell pipe whose JSON parse failed on the BOM, but apply_kb had already written. That added two extra copies of each of the three rows, in two forms: linked (N) and unlinked (X). I put rebuild_info/pitfalls.md back to its exact state after the first run, using a mechanical, assertion-checked script. It set the linked copies at lines 56, 156 and 165 back to the verdict's row text and deleted the 6 extra lines (57, 58, 174-177). I made no content judgement and edited no verdict. An in-memory re-application now shows 1 error (item-aim), 3 relinks and 3 re-inserts. That confirms the duplication bug and means nobody should rerun this step until apply_kb.py is fixed.

For the three link-* items, the intended linked text is the new_line in the verdict JSON; it is not applied yet. apply_kb.py index: errors=0 (10 rows inserted: battle, map_ai, movement, spell, chapter, cutscene, dialog, village, save, known_bugs). Link gate (check_mechanics.py --links): errors=0, no broken links on any of the three pages.

index.summary:
I wrote 10 index rows (battle, map_ai, movement, spell, chapter, cutscene, dialog, village, save, known_bugs) to workspace/game_mechanics/index_rows.json. The JSON loads cleanly as UTF-8. Each row follows the existing _index.md style: a link, then one line in Traditional Chinese listing what the page answers, built from its title, its verification scope and its section headings. I did not edit _index.md, README.md or rebuild_info/_index.md.

One statement these pages make false:
- README.md line 17 says program_info/ has "一檔對應一個子系統與 `src/` 模組" (each file maps to one subsystem and one src/ module). program_info/_index.md line 3 says the same thing ("一個檔對應一個子系統，之後也對應一個 `src/` 模組"). Two of the new pages break this. known_bugs.md is a cross-cutting list of bugs spanning more than a dozen src/ files and has no subsystem or module of its own. battle.md (combat.c, cmbblow.c, unitatk.c, unitstat.c, btlturn.c, death.c, unit.c, btlact.c) and spell.md each cover many src/ files. Some pages also split ownership of one src/ file: spell.md claims only some functions in unitstat.c and unit.c, and movement.md hands part of maptile.c to resource_info/map.md. The wording should become something like "one file per subsystem or cross-cutting topic, which may span several src/ files". The same fix applies to line 3 of program_info/_index.md, which the script does not touch.

I found nothing false in rebuild_info/_index.md. Its line 3 ("program_info/ 回答遊戲現在做什麼") still holds. The pitfalls.md row's "不能修的原版 bug" does not conflict with known_bugs.md: known_bugs.md owns the cause of each bug, and pitfalls.md owns how a rebuild would get it wrong. pitfalls.md already links to known_bugs.md and village.md.
